Explanation: Specific, testable behavior: position is either displayed or it is not. Update rate is handled separately by REQ-002.
Model requirement. Quantified threshold (500 ms) plus explicit operating modes. Use as a positive exemplar in the taxonomy.
Clear capability, directly testable.
Both 'safe' and 'efficient' are undefined. SWEHB names 'efficient' explicitly as a subjective term to avoid. SRS Open Items #1 confirms 'safe route' is unresolved.
Proposed Revision: Route criteria (keep-out distances, fuel/time optimization target) must be obtained from Flight Dynamics. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Trigger condition and action both stated.
'reasonably close' has no numeric tolerance, so no acceptance criterion can be written. Open Items #2 confirms.
Proposed Revision: Requires a maximum arrival miss-distance from Flight Dynamics. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: 'continuously monitor' specifies no sampling rate or staleness bound. A 1 Hz and a 1000 Hz implementation both satisfy the wording.
Proposed Revision: The SFMC shall sample main engine status at least once every [X] milliseconds. Rate must come from Propulsion.

Explanation: Exemplary: quantified threshold tied to a defined quantity (usable fuel capacity).
Threshold and both outputs are unambiguous and testable. Noted as compound only because two obligations share one ID, which affects verification tracking rather than clarity.
Proposed Revision: Optional: split into 009a (visual warning) and 009b (audible alarm) for traceability granularity.

Explanation: The trigger (engine failure) is defined but the required response is not. 'Appropriate corrective action' delegates a flight-safety design decision to the developer.
NASA Source: SWEHB 5.09 3.2.1 (Behavioral: defines behavior under specific conditions)
Proposed Revision: Requires the specific contingency sequence from Propulsion/Safety. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Testable given a defined sensor range.
Clear capability.
Enumerated list is complete and each field is testable. Compound only in the traceability sense - four display fields under one ID.
Proposed Revision: Optional: split per field for verification tracking.

Explanation: Safety-critical inhibit, clearly stated and testable.

'Friendly' is never defined; Open Items #10 admits friend-or-foe criteria are unresolved. A safety inhibit that depends on an undefined classification cannot be implemented or verified. Also conflicts with REQ-035 (see that row).
NASA Source: SWEHB 5.09 3.2.1 (Specific: clear and unambiguous) / NPR 7150.2D 4.1.4 (SWE-184: safety constraints in requirements documentation)
Proposed Revision: Requires friend-or-foe determination criteria from Mission Operations. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: 'Extremely accurate' has no metric or units. Open Items #7 confirms targeting accuracy is unresolved. Separately, the subject is 'the targeting system', not the SFMC - this may not be a software requirement at all.
Proposed Revision: Requires an accuracy figure and its units from Weapons/GNC, plus a decision on whether this is allocated to software. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Trigger and response both stated. No latency bound, but REQ-021 is where that gap is recorded.
'Clearly indicate' is subjective, and 'greatest danger' implies a threat-ranking function with no stated criteria (closure rate? weapon type? time to impact?).
Proposed Revision: Requires threat-prioritization criteria from Defensive Systems. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Mode-triggered action, testable.
Condition and action stated; 'when automatic defense is enabled' is a clear precondition.
Both 'quickly' and 'dangerous' are undefined, and 'respond' does not name an action. Three separate gaps in one sentence.
NASA Source: SWEHB 5.09 3.2.1 (Specific and verifiable/testable) / SWEHB 5.09 3.2.1 (Behavioral: defines behavior under specific conditions)
Proposed Revision: Requires a response-time bound and a threat-severity definition from Defensive Systems. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Clear capability.
Trigger and response stated.
Clear capability.

'Important' is undefined (Open Items #4) and 'securely encrypted' names no algorithm or standard. Also written in passive voice with no subject, so it is unclear the SFMC is the responsible component.
Proposed Revision: The SFMC shall encrypt all [defined category] communications using [named standard]. Requires classification criteria and a crypto standard from Cybersecurity. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Enumerated scope, testable.
Model requirement: trigger, response, and a 1-second latency bound.
Clear obligation.
Complete enumeration of required fields; each is testable.
Proposed Revision: Optional: split per field for traceability.

Explanation: 'Critical' is undefined (Open Items #3), and 'immediately' is unquantified - which also conflicts with REQ-027, where fault display is bounded at 1 second. Two requirements give different timing for overlapping behavior.
NASA Source: SWEHB 5.09 3.2.1 (Specific: clear and unambiguous) / NPR 7150.2D 4.1.6 (SWE-054: inconsistencies among requirements)
Proposed Revision: Requires a fault-criticality definition and a numeric bound. Should be reconciled with REQ-027. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Testable. Subject is the pilot rather than the SFMC, which is a minor style inconsistency, not a defect.

'Prioritize' names no mechanism (CPU scheduling? function shedding?) and 'nonessential' is undefined. Separately, life-support is NOT listed as an SFMC-connected subsystem in SRS section 1.2, so this requirement references a system the SFMC is not documented to control.
NASA Source: SWEHB 5.09 3.2.1 (Behavioral: defines behavior under specific conditions) / NPR 7150.2D 4.1.6 (SWE-054: inconsistencies among requirements)
Proposed Revision: Requires a function-priority table and clarification of whether life-support is within SFMC scope. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: 'Seriously damaged' and 'safest destination' are both undefined. Open Items #5 confirms 'safe location' is unresolved.
Proposed Revision: Requires damage-assessment thresholds and destination-safety criteria. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: 'Safe location' undefined (Open Items #5). 'Shall be capable of' states a capability rather than a behavior, which is weaker than 'shall fly'. Also overlaps REQ-033 and REQ-005 without stating how they interact.
NASA Source: SWEHB 5.09 3.2.1 (Behavioral: defines behavior under specific conditions)
Proposed Revision: The SFMC shall fly the spacecraft to a destination meeting [criteria] when [condition]. Requires criteria from Mission Operations. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: 'Always' is an unbounded absolute. More seriously, it directly conflicts with REQ-015: if the pilot can ALWAYS override automatic controls, can the pilot override the friendly-fire inhibit? The two requirements cannot both hold as written. This is the clearest example in the SRS of an inconsistency detectable only by reading the set.
Proposed Revision: Requires an explicit statement of which safety inhibits are non-overridable. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Quantified (30 s) and testable. 'Operational' is not formally defined, but boot-to-ready is a reasonable reading.
'Without noticeable delay' is subjective and observer-dependent. Open Items #8 confirms.
Proposed Revision: Requires a latency ceiling in milliseconds from Human Systems Integration. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Quantified (10 Hz), which is good. But REQ-002 requires position updates at only 2 Hz (500 ms). If displayed position is 'flight information', the two requirements specify different rates for the same data.
Proposed Revision: Reconcile with REQ-002: define whether 'flight information' includes position, and state one rate.

Explanation: Quantified duration, testable.
'Never crash' is a universal negative and cannot be demonstrated by finite testing. Reliability must be expressed statistically or against a defined operational profile.
Proposed Revision: The SFMC software shall exhibit no more than [X] unplanned terminations per [Y] operating hours. Requires a reliability target from Systems Engineering.

Explanation: 'Recoverable' is defined only by the fact that recovery is possible, making the requirement circular. No recovery time bound is given either.
Proposed Revision: Requires an enumerated fault taxonomy identifying which classes are recoverable, plus a maximum recovery time. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: 'Important mission data' is undefined. Same undefined qualifier as REQ-025, applied to a different subsystem.
Proposed Revision: Requires a data-classification scheme naming which items must survive a fault. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: 'Whenever possible' makes the requirement unfalsifiable - any failure to continue operating can be attributed to it not being possible.
Proposed Revision: Requires an explicit degraded-mode matrix: which subsystem losses require which continued functions.

Explanation: Clear obligation; contents are specified in REQ-045.
Complete enumeration of six event classes, each individually testable. Compound in the traceability sense only.
Proposed Revision: Optional: split into 045a-045f so partial implementation can be recorded.

Explanation: Clear and testable.
'Sufficient storage' gives no capacity figure and no worst-case event rate to derive one from. Open Items #6 confirms.
Proposed Revision: Requires a worst-case event-rate estimate and a resulting capacity in MB/GB, for the 72-hour mission of REQ-039. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Clear precondition on spacecraft operation, testable.
Testable given a defined authorization scheme; REQ-048 provides adjacent context.
'State-of-the-art' names no standard and changes meaning over time, so the same implementation could pass today and fail later. Open Items #9 confirms.
Proposed Revision: Requires named standards (e.g. a FIPS or CCSDS reference) from Cybersecurity. Cannot revise without stakeholder input - see Explanation.

Explanation: Legitimate design constraint, clearly stated.
Legitimate interface constraint.
Testable, with a clear mode precondition. Subject is maintenance personnel rather than the SFMC - minor style inconsistency only.
Clear obligation with a defined ordering ('before installing').
